BRAINS resume root package comprises 373 files and is explicitly NOT counted in this tranche.

license.obligation: Preserve Greg Borden copyright and MIT notice in copied source.

historical_scan.interpretation: Top-of-file Python scanner flag does not by itself prove malware. Three subprocess flags are in local pytest CLI tests. The pinned source has all 21 owned files; family references to siblings outside the package remain separate and do not authorize host behavior.

material_findings.finding: Input like '180-220k' is listed as supported, but parser reads 180 and 220k as separate amounts without propagating shared suffix: resulting min 180 and max 220000. This can distort pay-floor filters and market-median conclusions.

The scorer coerces Python floats including NaN/infinity without isfinite validation; _clamp comparisons do not reject NaN, allowing nonfinite weighted scores or meaningless recommendations. Regression tests cover numeric range but not nonfinite inputs.

Normalizing job titles deletes 'senior', 'lead', 'staff', 'principal' and grade tokens. Same company, location and base title can merge distinct seniority-level openings into one posting, hiding a potentially better legitimate opportunity.

Skill reads private resume/profile and workspace decisions, writes scored postings and tells host to render HTML from untrusted public posting text. No explicit data-minimization, HTML escaping, or approval of local destination is enforced by these source instructions. Search results must remain untrusted, and no auto-apply/messaging authority follows.

Rubric says direct ATS and recent dates are 'legitimate by default' and combines heuristics with quoted market prevalence. A posted listing is not proof of funded vacancy; the bundled outcome eval assertions are largely passed=false, not observed host acceptance.

positive_safeguards: Separates vacancy legitimacy from candidate match and maintains company/board source attribution and dated link checks.
Respects explicit user criteria, excludes auto-applying/sending, carries severe job scam red flags, and warns about private employer ATS information.
Uses subprocess tests only for local scoring CLI tests and bounded Python scripts; no obvious malicious network calls in the owned executable files.
Includes targeted tests for score weights and query-builder construction, though those do not cover identified corner cases.
reasoned_cases: Input 180-220k: regex parses first amount as 180 and second as 220000, not the advertised 180000-220000 range.
Python float('nan') accepted by _coerce_float and unchanged by _clamp; nonfinite weighted result is not a valid job score.
Senior Engineer and Principal Engineer at same company and location normalize to same title key, risking a false duplicate.
Posting HTML supplied by a job board must be escaped and never used as agent instructions or automatic apply permission.
records.remediation: Propagate suffix units across salary ranges with fixtures, reject nonfinite scores, preserve seniority in dedupe identity or require a separate unique job ID, safely escape HTML and obtain workspace/data-source permission, and keep legitimacy as probabilistic evidence rather than verified funding.

historical_scan.interpretation: An AR2 scanner finding at 190 does not establish malware. The included Blender verification block can destructively clear a scene and is a real source-side risk in a nonisolated host.

material_findings.finding: Runnable verification calls clear_scene() with bpy.ops.object.select_all and bpy.ops.object.delete, deleting all current-scene objects. The documented shell example uses --factory-startup in a separate headless process, which mitigates the standard path, but adapting/running it inside a user's open .blend context can destroy existing work without permission or backup.

Signed-volume sum takes only vertices [0],[1],[2] of each polygon, excluding the second triangle of quad and polygon faces. It may substantially undercount signed volume and provide unreliable normals/volume checks while reporting PASS. The source's '24 checks, 0 failed' output is an unreplicated historical claim.
Applied-scale check tests abs(abs(s)-1), accepting scale (-1,1,1) even though the stated pass rule is scale==(1,1,1); negative scale/mirrors can alter handedness and face winding.

The allowed-tools Bash and direct Blender interpreter example require explicit scope to run and separate scratch scenes; source instructions alone do not grant authority to write or export a user scene.

positive_safeguards: Provides a clear connection-map method and mathematical checks for mesh dimension/orientation/joins.
The example deliberately uses --background --factory-startup, mitigating destruction when run unchanged as a new isolated Blender process.
No external service, credential harvest or remote write is embedded in the one-file skill.
reasoned_cases: Running the sample in a live user scene deletes all objects; the documented factory-startup CLI avoids that only when followed exactly.
A Blender quad has four vertices but volume formula consumes only three; actual signed volume differs from the checked value.
Scale -1 on an axis satisfies abs(abs(s)-1)<1e-6 despite requiring scale (1,1,1).
records.remediation: Clearly prohibit executing the sample in an active .blend scene; require empty isolated temporary scene and explicit backup for any scene mutation; triangulate polygons or use a trusted evaluated-mesh volume API; reject negative scale; verify expected volume/geometry numerically.

Optional inklecate compile run is proposed whenever available, without distinguishing read-only static checking from a permitted local subprocess and generated output. Requires explicit host/runtime scope and path controls.

The skill asks to check all route orderings and deadlocks but supplies no explicit state-space bound, deterministic route selection or time budget. In large branching IF, 'complete route coverage' is not defensible without observed traversal and reported frontier limits.
Ink source and in-world dialogue may contain prompt-shaped text; treat as data, not authority to write outside the review directory.
